51494458.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human RXRalpha LBD (T225 to T462 residues) assessed as binding constant by isothermal titration calorimetry
51494458.references_previous: Xia, G.; Boerma, L. J.; Cox, B. D.; Qiu, C.; Kang, S.; Smith, C. D.; Renfrow, M. B.; Muccio, D. Structure, energetics, and dynamics of binding coactivator peptide to the human retinoid X receptor alpha ligand binding domain complex with 9-cis-retinoic acid. Biochemistry 2011, 50, 93–105.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - ITC Measurements: ITC experiments were performed using an Auto-iTC200 system (Malvern Instruments, Westborough, MA) to measure the binding of the GRIP-1 coactivator peptide to holo-hRXRα-LBD homodimers, as described previously.16 The ITC sample cell contained 20–25 μM of hRXRα-LBD homodimers in 20 mM tris, pH 8.0, 50 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA, 2 mM DTT, and 50 μM each of rexinoids 3–6 in dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) solution. The ITC syringe contained 0.5–0.6 mM of GRIP-1 peptide in the same buffer. Each titration experiment consisted of 20 injections of 2.0 μL of GRIP-1 into the holo-hRXRα-LBD homodimers at 25 °C. Background mixing heat was determined from injections of GRIP-1 into the same buffer without protein or rexinoids. Data analysis was performed using the built-in analysis module in Origin 7 provided by the ITC manufacturer. The monomeric protein concentration was used for obtaining the stoichiometry of GRIP-1 binding to each RXRα-LBD monomer.
original_paragraph.Table 2 Caption: Summary of ITC Measurements of GRIP-1 Binding to hRXRα-LBD:Ligand Complexes at 25 °C
original_paragraph.Results Section - 2.3: To provide in vitro evaluation of agonist activity, we determined the thermodynamics of the coactivator peptide GRIP-1 binding to hRXRα-LBD homodimers containing saturating amounts of ligands 3–6. These studies were undertaken to decide if analogs 3–6 were able to recruit coactivator peptide to the surface of the LBD of the RXR receptor consistent with agonist activity. The thermodynamic signature of the coactivator peptide binding is characteristic of agonist activity.15,19 Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) measurements were performed at 25 °C (Table 2). GRIP-1 bound well to hRXRα-LBD homodimers containing each of the ligands 3–6 (stoichiometry of binding nearly 1 for GRIP-1:hRXRα-LBD monomer subunit). The GRIP-1 binding affinities, binding enthalpies, entropies, and free-energy changes were nearly identical to those complexes containing ligands 3, 4, or 6. For an RXR-LBD homodimer complex containing bound 5, the binding affinity and free-energy change were nearly identical to the other ligands, but the binding free energy contained an entropy contribution (Table 2). The results from both transactivation and ITC studies indicated that ligands 3–6 were potent agonists.
